correctness.rationale: For n>=5 the cylindrical ladder and crossed-seam Möbius ladder have 2n vertices and three incident edges per vertex. A Hamiltonian cycle with a proper nonempty set S of chosen rungs forces omitted horizontal edges in paired adjacent cuts; r such disjoint cuts yield exactly r disjoint circuits, so Hamiltonian cases with such support have exactly one paired cut and n corresponding two-rung cycles. No-rung support is Hamiltonian only in Möbius ladder (one perimeter cycle); full-rung support produces exactly two Hamiltonian cycles for even cylindrical ladder or odd Möbius ladder, none otherwise. All simple 4-cycles for n>=5 are rung squares, and any two-edge Hamiltonian switch is an alternating four-cycle. The Möbius rim swaps with each one-cut cycle, other moves either disconnect or are locally impossible; cylindrical cycles are isolated, and Möbius odd full-rung cycles isolated. Independent fresh perfect-matching-complement enumeration for n=5..9, including every pairwise symmetric-difference-of-4 adjacency, matched nK1, (n+2)K1, K1,n and K1,n plus 2K1 exactly. The proof, not enumeration, handles all n>=5.
